title: Oliver Glasner defends Crystal Palace right to rotate vs. Manchester City, Arsenal
content:
Oliver Glasner has defended his right to rotate his Crystal Palace team for their games against Premier League title contenders Manchester City and Arsenal.

The south-London side could have a significant say in the Premier League title race as they face City at the Etihad on May 13 and league leaders Arsenal at Selhurst Park on the final day of the season on May 24.

That game is just three days before Palace’s Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano at the Red Bull Arena in Leipzig on May 27.

The Palace manager said it would be “nonsense” to criticise him for rotating and argued that at the conclusion of a 38-game season “everybody gets what they deserve”.

“I don’t know what we’re doing yet,” Glasner said when asked about the possibility of resting players before the final. “Maybe we’ll be playing with the same line-up that we’ll play against Rayo.

“It feels like the league title (may be) decided on the last day, but at the end, it’s a result of 38 matchdays and everybody gets what they deserve. To be honest, if somebody criticises (me for this), it would be nonsense.

“It’s (not) just the last game. There were 37 games played before and that means if another team rotated against City or Arsenal, they affected the title race as well.

“I’m not responsible for Arsenal, and I’m not responsible for Manchester City. I’m responsible for Crystal Palace, and I get paid for doing the best things for Crystal Palace.”

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League, having played a game more than second-placed City.

In addition to City’s game against Palace, Pep Guardiola’s side host Brentford on Saturday and travel to the Vitality Stadium to face Bournemouth. That game will be played on May 19, three days after the FA Cup final. They then end their season at home to Aston Villa.

Arsenal travel to the London Stadium to face West Ham United on Sunday. They then host Burnley on May 18 before concluding their league season against Palace. Mikel Arteta’s side will compete in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain six days later, on May 30.

Glasner’s side confirmed their pathway to the Conference League final via a 2-1 victory over Shakhtar Donetsk on Thursday.
